title: Statistical Assistants
description: Compile and compute data according to statistical formulas for use in statistical studies. May perform actuarial computations and compile charts and graphs for use by actuaries. Includes actuarial clerks.

tasks.text: Check source data to verify completeness and accuracy.
Compile reports, charts, or graphs that describe and interpret findings of analyses.
Organize paperwork, such as survey forms or reports, for distribution or analysis.
Check survey responses for errors, such as the use of pens instead of pencils, and set aside response forms that cannot be used.
Compile statistics from source materials, such as production or sales records, quality-control or test records, time sheets, or survey sheets.
Enter data into computers for use in analyses or reports.
File data and related information, and maintain and update databases.
Code data prior to computer entry, using lists of codes.
Compute and analyze data, using statistical formulas and computers or calculators.
Interview people and keep track of their responses.
Participate in the publication of data or information.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Programming

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Persuasion

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C#, C++, Oracle Java, Python.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Benfield ReMetrica, Data visualization software, IBM SPSS Statistics, Insightful S-PLUS.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database software, dBASE, Microsoft Access, QSR International NVivo.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: A programming language APL, Microsoft Visual Basic, Microsoft Visual Studio, Software development tools.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Google Workspace software, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: IBM Lotus 1-2-3, Microsoft Excel.
